findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so recorded calls are lost
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new instance, so the `Info` call is recorded on a throwaway logger and never on the original. Any test that injects a `TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and checks `InfoLogs.Calls` or `Ctx` would see nothing. `New` has the same limitation. The fake should return the receiver, or share its state.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the reworked LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: Plugin ID, endpoint, datasource name/UID, user, and traceID used to be logged explicitly by LoggerMiddleware. They now depend on ContextualLoggerMiddleware putting them into the context and on `FromContext` picking them up. Nothing tests either part. The renamed metrics test only checks metrics. A regression, such as a middleware ordering change or `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` hitting its fallback, would silently drop these fields from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops context when the type assertion fails
findings.body: If `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` does not return a `*log.ConcreteLogger`, the code falls back to `d.New()`. The returned logger then has none of the contextual attributes (plugin ID, endpoint, datasource, traceID). The request log line would lose these fields with no error or warning. Before this PR they were added explicitly by LoggerMiddleware, so this is a quiet regression risk.
